name: Thyroglossal Duct Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Thyroglossal Duct Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a painless, midline neck mass typically located near the hyoid bone
Mass moves upward on protrusion of the tongue or swallowing
Ultrasound or CT imaging showing cystic lesion in the midline neck along the thyroglossal duct tract
No signs of acute infection or abscess formation in the cyst
Normal thyroid function tests and presence of normal thyroid gland in usual location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a painless midline neck mass that moves with tongue protrusion plus imaging confirmation of a cystic lesion along the thyroglossal duct tract
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Fine needle aspiration cytology may be used to exclude malignancy or infection

occasional.symptomName: Infection of the cyst presenting with erythema and swelling

rare.notes: Rare papillary thyroid carcinoma arising in cyst

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation from cyst to skin
Recurrent cyst formation after incomplete excision

laboratory: Possible elevated inflammatory markers if infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing anechoic or hypoechoic cystic lesion in midline neck
CT or MRI demonstrating cystic mass along thyroglossal duct tract
Normal thyroid gland location confirmed by imaging
other: Fine needle aspiration cytology may show benign cystic contents or exclude malignancy
Movement of mass with tongue protrusion on physical exam

distinguishingFeatures: Does not move with tongue protrusion
Does not move with tongue protrusion
Does not move with tongue protrusion
May have altered thyroid function tests

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of neck mass
Signs of infection such as fever, erythema, and tenderness
Fixation of mass to surrounding tissues
references: Nussbaum M, et al. Thyroglossal duct cyst: clinical features and surgical management. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2019.
Smith MM, et al. Imaging of congenital neck masses in children. Radiographics. 2020.
American Thyroid Association Guidelines for Thyroid Nodules and Differentiated Thyroid Cancer, 2015.
